newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle near standstill - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle near standstill - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade was near a standstill, with slaughter steers and heifers not tested, feedlot sources said.
Owners priced cattle at $65.00 to $66.00 in anticipation of firm demand from packers looking to fill beef orders booked by retailers earlier in the month, they said.
Bids were light and scattered from $62.00 to $63.00 following sales last week at $64.00, which were $2.00 higher than the previous week, the feedlot sources said.
Fed cattle prices were seen underpinned by higher beef prices and outlooks for slowly declining cattle stocks.
Supplies of market-ready cattle were seen waning into the fall, several feedlot sources said.
Beef prices at midday were quoted up $0.16 to $0.35 per cwt, with 46 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA statistics showed. Heavyweight choice beef was quoted at $101.96, up $0.34 from Friday.

Nebraska feedlot sales also inactive, with bids at $103.00-$104.00 per cwt on a dressed basis passed by owners asking $106.00-$107.00. Brisk sales last week were mostly at $104.00, with a few at $105.00.
